deities: Lord Shiva (svayambhu Shivling in the main cave)

history.dynasty: None — founded in modern times by saint Shri Mahant Narayandas Ji Tyagi
history.summary: The cave shrine was discovered in 1949 by Shri Mahant Narayandas Ji Tyagi (sources render the name variously as Narayandas/Narayan Das) and reconstruction work was done by him on 2 April 1965. The hilltop complex at Lalghati contains seven natural caves, one of which houses a svayambhu (self-manifested) Shivling fed by a natural water source that never dries up. Below the cave are tableaux of Radha-Krishna and Ram-Janaki-Lakshman; the complex also holds an old Hanuman shrine, a Durga shrine and a Sanskrit college. FLAG: yometro.com claims the temple was 'built in 1947 by Shri Ramesh Bhai Ojha' — this conflicts with the 1949-discovery account given by most sources and is flagged as unverified.

name: Gufa Mandir
town_description: Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh, is known as the City of Lakes for its two artificial lakes (Upper and Lower) built centuries ago. It is one of India's greenest cities, blending Nawabi heritage — mosques, palaces and bazaars — with modern institutions and museums.

travel.airport: Raja Bhoj International Airport, Bhopal (~7 km; verify)
travel.road: On Gufa Mandir Rd / Nevri Mandir Marg, Lalghati (Nayapura), Bhopal; reachable by bus, taxi and auto-rickshaw
